intro.text: This page describes the network architecture of the API Hub and the certificates that secure communication between all parties in the ecosystem.

sections.heading: Connectivity between TPPs, Hub, and LFI

blocks.text: The diagram below shows the full connectivity model between TPPs, the API Hub, and the LFI's infrastructure.

All connections between the API Hub and external parties use mutual TLS (mTLS). Each certificate has a specific role in securing a particular connection path. The certificates are created and stored within the Trust Framework, and the private keys are held by the party responsible for that connection.
The sequence diagram below shows which certificate secures each direction of traffic between the TPP, the API Hub, and the LFI's Ozone Connect backend.

rows: The TPP presents its client certificate to identify itself to the API Hub.
The API Hub presents this server certificate to identify the LFI's API Hub instance to the TPP.
The TPP signs request JWTs (e.g. PAR request objects and private_key_jwt client assertions) sent to the API Hub. The API Hub verifies using the public key in the TPP's JWKS.
The API Hub signs responses and id_token payloads sent to the TPP. The TPP verifies using the public key in the JWKS.
The API Hub presents this client certificate when calling the LFI's Ozone Connect endpoints.
The LFI's Ozone Connect server presents this certificate to identify itself to the API Hub.
The API Hub signs JWT Auth headers on Ozone Connect requests. Only applicable when JWT Auth is selected.
The LFI signs JWT Auth headers on Ozone Connect responses. Only applicable when JWT Auth is selected.

subsections.heading: LFI to API Hub (Consent Manager & Headless Heimdall)

rows: The LFI presents this client certificate when calling the Consent Manager and Headless Heimdall Auth Server.
The Consent Manager and Headless Heimdall servers present this certificate to identify themselves to the LFI.
The LFI signs JWT Auth headers on requests to the Consent Manager and Headless Heimdall. Only applicable when JWT Auth is selected.
The API Hub signs JWT Auth headers on Consent Manager and Headless Heimdall responses. Only applicable when JWT Auth is selected.

sections.heading: JWE encryption keys for sensitive payloads

blocks.text: Payload encryption is separate from transport: Enc1 and Enc2 are JWE keys applied to the message body, not to the TLS connection. The sequence below shows how each one is used.

rows: Used by the TPP to encrypt Personally Identifiable Information (PII) sent via the API Hub. Only the LFI can decrypt this data using its private key.
Used by the API Hub to encrypt webhook event payloads sent to the TPP. Only the TPP can decrypt using its private key.

blocks.text: When creating these certificates in the Trust Framework, select the following types:

items: C1, C3, C4 — OPF UAE CLIENT TRANSPORT
S1, S3, S4 — OPF UAE SERVER TRANSPORT
Sig1, Sig2, Sig3, Sig4 — OPF UAE CLIENT SIGNING

blocks.text: The Sig3 and Sig4 certificates are only required when JWT Auth is selected as the application layer authentication method.

subsections.heading: Ozone-held certificates (S1, S3, Sig2, C4, Sig3)

blocks.text: For certificates where Ozone holds the private key, the process is:

items: Ozone generates the private key and a Certificate Signing Request (CSR).

For S1, S3, and Sig2: Ozone provides the CSR to the LFI. The LFI uploads the CSR to their own organisation in the Trust Framework to generate the certificate, then provides the JWKS URL and KID back to Ozone.
For C4 and Sig3: These certificates are in Ozone's own Trust Framework organisation. Ozone provides the JWKS URL and KID to the LFI. No action is required from the LFI for these certificates.

blocks.text: For certificates where the LFI holds the private key, the process is:

items: The LFI generates the private key and CSR.
For C3 and Sig4: The LFI creates the certificate in the C3-hh-cm-client application in the Trust Framework. See Creating the C3-hh-cm-client Application and Keys & Certificates.
For S4 and Enc1: The LFI creates the certificate under Organisation Certificates in the Trust Framework.
The LFI provides the JWKS URL and KID to Ozone.

blocks.text: If your institution operates multiple API Hub instances (e.g. for retail and business brands), LFI-held certificates (C3, S4, Sig4, Enc1) MAY be reused across brands. Each brand still requires its own environment-specific onboarding form, but can reference the same certificates if appropriate.

items: Environment Specific Configuration — the onboarding form where all certificate details are exchanged
Application Layer Authentication — choose your application layer authentication method (determines whether Sig3/Sig4 are required)
Keys & Certificates — how to generate keys and upload CSRs in the Trust Framework
